title: Affinity-aware slice prefetch and kernel scoring for heterogeneous GPUs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We observe tail-latency spikes and throughput cliffs on mixed-tenant MIG/L40S/A10 clusters when servicing workloads with heterogenous sequence lengths. The current kernel chooser biases toward single-kernel throughput but ignores slice-affinity (how a request maps to a MIG slice topology) and transient GPU clock/thermal state. This causes suboptimal kernel pairing for prefill vs decode phases, KV cache warm-up stalls, and occasional thermal-driven clock downshifts that amplify latency variance.

Goal: Implement an affinity-aware kernel scoring layer and a staggered prefetch pipeline that: (1) factors MIG slice topology, NVLink locality, and active clock-state into kernel selection scores, (2) separates prefill-prefetch priorities between short/long prompts to reduce KV cache churn, and (3) applies thermal hysteresis to avoid repeated clock transitions during bursty load. The feature should be rollout-safe (canary + auto-fallback) and have observable metrics in Console for token-latency by slice and kernel-class.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile token latency reduced by >=12% on mixed-length workloads in H100 MIG test harness compared to baseline (same model, same batch policy)
95th-percentile prefill latency variance reduced by >=20% across L40S cluster runs under synthetic burst traffic
No throughput regression (>5%) on dedicated A10 benchmarks at target batch sizes
Automated integration tests covering: kernel score calculation, slice-affinity decision, and prefetch pipeline behavior added to CI
Canary rollout plan documented and console dashboards updated to show token-level latency by kernel and slice
updates: 2025-11-03: Initial spike analysis completed using hw-telemetry traces from prod-replay; identified correlation between clock downshifts and large prefill bursts on mixed-MIG nodes.

2025-11-05: Design review with runtime/infra. Decided on additive scoring model (latency_estimate + slice_penalty + clock_penalty) instead of multiplicative to keep scores interpretable for debugging.

2025-11-07: Microbenchmarks (local H100 dev rig, MIG 7g.20gb) show 14% 95p token-latency improvement when using slice-affinity weights and staggered prefetch for long prompts. Baseline: runtime-1.20 kernel selection.
2025-11-09: Prototype implemented behind feature-flag (slice_affinity_prefetch=true). Added telemetry hooks for kernel_id, slice_id, chosen_score, and clock_state. Short demo recorded and uploaded.

2025-11-11: Peer review from kernel-engineering (Liam Brooks) requested rework: reduce dependency on static table lookups for slice_penalty; prefer runtime-derived heuristics to adapt to noisy telemetry. Working on hybrid approach.
2025-11-12: Submitted PR for initial scorer + prefetch pipeline (see related_prs). Preparing a canary test plan against dedicated staging cluster.
notes: Trade-offs: More complex scoring adds CPU overhead in the router; we profile and cap scorer time at 50us/request. If cap exceeded, fallback to legacy chooser.
Thermal hysteresis: implement a 8-second hold window after a clock increase before allowing another clock step-down to avoid oscillation during bursty traffic.
Prefetch policy: two-tier pipeline: priority-0 for short prompts (<=64 tokens) allowing immediate prefill, priority-1 for long prompts staggered with 2-3ms spacing to smooth KV cache pressure.
Fallbacks: On overloaded nodes, prefer decode-friendly kernels that minimize warm-cache misses even if per-token throughput is slightly lower.
Benchmarks: H100 (MIG 7g.20gb) mixed synthetic set: baseline 95p=230ms -> prototype 95p=198ms. L40S multi-tenant runs showed 18% reduction in prefill variance.

Open questions: how to encode NVLink locality score for multi-GPU models without adding expensive topology queries to the fast path? Proposal: cache topology per pod and update on topology-change events.
review_feedback: Liam Brooks (kernel-engineering): Prefer runtime heuristics over static penalties; ensure scorer can be sampled and replayed for offline debugging.
Priya Nair (SRE): Add alert when scorer latency >50us for 1m to avoid adding jitter to API path.
Ruben Alvarez (product): Expose an opt-out knob for customers on Dedicated that want stable single-kernel behavior for deterministic latency
